Application Materials.content:
For your application you will need:
- Personal details
- Transcripts and certificates of any essential qualifications
- Referee details
- A personal statement (if applicable to your chosen course)
- Your Queen’s student ID if you are a current / former student
**If you have completed your qualification, you should upload your degree award certificate and degree transcript. If you have not yet completed your degree, please upload your transcript to show results to date.**
International applicants must scan and upload supporting documents along with the application. Queen’s may not be able to make a decision until all relevant documents have been received. Please upload good quality scanned copies of:
- Degree transcripts for all completed periods of study (undergraduate level and above).
- If your degree is still in progress, a transcript of results achieved to date.
- Copies of official Degree/Diploma Certificates for qualifications already completed.
- Certified translations if original documents are not in English; if unavailable at application, forward them by email to [student@qub.ac.uk](mailto:intl.student@qub.ac.uk) when available.
For all applications (Postgraduate Taught and Research), applicants must include the names and contact details of **two referees**, normally academics familiar with undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies. If you have taken a higher degree or postgraduate course recently, one referee should be from that institution. If you have been away from higher education for some time, you may use an employer as one referee. You do not need to include reference letters with your application; these will be requested directly by the University if required.

Application Deadlines.content: Applicants are advised to apply as early as possible and ideally no later than **14th August 2026** for courses which commence in **late September**. In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Normally a **strong 2.2 Honours degree or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in any discipline**.
- Queen's Business School welcomes applications from a diverse range of backgrounds and may consider **previous managerial work experience alongside lower academic qualifications**.
- For applicants from **China Mainland**: applicants should hold a good four-year bachelor degree from a recognised, well ranked university. For a programme requiring a **UK 2.2 Hons standard**, the stated China Mainland thresholds are:
| Type of institution | UK 2.2 Hons standard |
| --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | Final average **70%** |
| Tier 2 | Final average **75%** |
| Tier 3 | Final average **80%** |
**Tier 1:** Prestigious Universities (Double First Class Universities and Top 100 Academic Ranking of World Universities). **Tier 2:** Other Recognised Universities and Independent Colleges affiliated to a Tier 1 Institution (as defined by Queen's). **Tier 3:** Other Independent Colleges recognised by Ministry of Education and Self-Study Degrees.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Evidence of an **IELTS score of 6.5, with not less than 5.5 in any component**, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required. IELTS must be **taken within the last 2 years**.
International students wishing to apply to Queen's University Belfast, and for whom English is not their first language, must demonstrate proficiency in English. Non-EEA nationals must also satisfy UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) English language requirements for visa purposes. More information is available at [www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs](https://www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs).
If English language skills need to be improved before entry, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers:
- [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English): an intensive English language and study skills course for successful university study at degree level.
- [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English): a short intensive academic English course for students starting a degree programme at Queen's University Belfast who need to improve their English.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is a one-year full-time programme that prepares students for the data-driven marketing landscape by combining strategic marketing expertise with digital and analytical capabilities. The programme develops proficiency in leveraging analytics tools and creating evidence-based marketing solutions that drive measurable business impact. Through applied learning including industry projects and capstone research, it equips marketing graduates with the technical and strategic competencies required to lead digital transformation initiatives and optimise marketing performance in contemporary organisations.
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics programme offers students the opportunity to engage directly with industry through the Capstone Dissertation's dual-pathway approach. Students can undertake an Applied Marketing Project working with industry partners to address real organisational challenges, benefiting from industry mentorship and collaborative problem-solving. Or they can apply for a competitive industry placement within a company, agency, or marketing department. The programme is further enriched through regular guest speakers from leading industry professionals, live case study-led assessments, and networking opportunities with industry practitioners, alumni, and peers.
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is delivered at Queen's Business School through in-person instruction, combining traditional lectures with student-focused workshops and hands-on practical classes. The course can only be taken on a full-time basis. Students undertake 4 modules in semester 1 and a further 4 in semester 2. In semester 3, students undertake the Capstone module. Students who successfully complete eight taught modules (120 CATS) and the Capstone module (60 CATS) are awarded an MSc in Digital Marketing and Analytics degree. Other exit qualifications available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing 120 CATS from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing 60 CATS from taught modules.
Semester 3 is a 60 CATS Capstone Dissertation module. The Capstone Dissertation represents an independent piece of research with the opportunity to apply knowledge and skills acquired over previous semesters to design, develop, and propose marketing solutions for real-world business or societal challenges. Students have two pathways to choose from: (i) Applied Marketing Project, working on an organisation; or (ii) Industry Placement Project, working in an organisation.
Classes will be delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops and they will be interactive and discussion-based, blending theory with practical examples. Learning and engagement approaches include case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through the capstone projects where students choose between different pathways. Students are assigned dedicated academic support for these projects and company mentors where relevant. There are 4 taught classes per week, 3 hours each. Additional academic and employability support classes are timetabled throughout the week.
People teaching you: [Dr Grace Carson](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/grace-carson-2), Programme Director, Queen's Business School.
The programme prepares graduates for high-demand careers in specialised roles such as Digital Marketing Manager, Customer Insights Specialist, Marketing Performance Analyst, Social Media Strategist, Marketing Analytics Consultant, and Brand Development Manager. Graduates will be equipped to drive digital transformation initiatives, optimise campaign performance through data analytics, and lead marketing innovation across diverse industries including technology, retail, financial services, healthcare, and digital agencies. Graduates from this programme have secured roles with employers such as PwC, BBC, Marriott International, Warner Brothers, ASOS, Primark, Selfridges, Yahoo, Amazon, and many others.
Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/).

Curriculum.content:
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is a **one-year full-time programme** delivered at Queen's Business School through **in-person instruction**, combining traditional lectures with student-focused workshops and hands-on practical classes. The course can only be taken on a **full-time basis**. Students undertake **4 modules in semester 1** and **4 in semester 2**. Students who successfully complete **eight taught modules (120 CATS)** and the **Capstone module (60 CATS)** in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Digital Marketing and Analytics degree. Other exit qualifications available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing **120 CATS** from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing **60 CATS** from taught modules.
- **Semester 1:** structured through a **60 CATS** package consisting of **4 core modules**, each worth **15 CATS**: Digital Marketing Principles and Practice; Marketing Management; Digital Business Strategy; Generative AI and Business Intelligence.
- **Semester 2:** structured through a **60 CATS** package consisting of **2 core modules**, each worth **15 CATS**, and an additional **2 15 CAT modules**, selected from 4 options.
- **Semester 2 core modules:** Consumer Behaviour in the Digital Age; Marketing Analytics.
- **Semester 2 optional modules:** Strategy, Change and Analytics; Social Media and Reputation Management; AI Frontiers; Cyber Security & Digital Risk Management.
- **Semester 3:** a **60 CATS Capstone Dissertation module**. The Capstone Dissertation is an independent piece of research applying knowledge and skills acquired over previous semesters to design, develop, and propose marketing solutions for real-world business or societal challenges.
- The Capstone Dissertation has two applied pathways: **Applied Marketing Project (working on an organisation)**, where students conduct an independent research project analysing and proposing solutions to specific digital marketing challenges faced by a real organisation/s; or **Industry Placement Project (working in an organisation)**, where students undertake a placement within a company, agency, or marketing department, conducting research that directly informs their host organisation's marketing strategy and operations.
- Classes are delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops, interactive and discussion-based, blending theory with practical examples. Learning and engagement approaches include case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through the capstone projects.
- **Teaching times:** 4 taught classes per week, 3 hours each. Additional academic and employability support classes are timetabled throughout the week.

Financial Aid.content:
**Scholarships of £6000 available exclusively for outstanding international applicants studying postgraduate taught programmes at Queen’s Business School in the academic year 2026/27.**
- Applicants must hold an offer to study a postgraduate taught programme at Queen’s Business School. **No application necessary.** If eligible, confirmation of your award will be issued with your offer.
- The **Queen’s Business School Scholarship** is available only to new students who hold an offer for a place on a **full-time postgraduate taught programme at the Queen’s Business School**, starting in the academic year 2026/27 and prior to commencement of study have met any academic and language conditions attached to their offer.
- Students must be classified as international fee-paying students paying the full international tuition fee rate. Students paying NI, ROI, EU or GB fees are not eligible.
- The discount is awarded for the first year of study only and is deducted from **gross** tuition fees upon enrolment.
- Students must be self-funded i.e. the tuition fees are being paid by yourself or your parents at the full international tuition fee rate.
- If you are in receipt of funding from an external sponsorship body such as Government, a charity or a private organisation you will not be eligible for a Queen’s Business School Scholarship 2026/27.
- International scholarships cannot be used in conjunction with any other University tuition fee scholarship. Where **eligible** students can however use their scholarship in conjunction with the Early Confirmation Award or the ISC Scholarship.
- The University is unable to consider requests for increased and/or further funding. The amount of scholarship offered is non-negotiable.

Multiple Applications.content:
After you have entered the core details about yourself and your academic background, you can apply for one or multiple courses.
If you have applied for and been offered a place on more than one programme of study, you must indicate whether you wish to accept or decline the offer against each programme. Given that your final programme choice may be dependent on funding and/or other factors, you may initially decide to accept more than one offer of a place.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Applications for deferred entry may be permitted. However, in considering requests for deferred entry it will be necessary to consider if the course will be offered in a subsequent year or, in the case of research, the research project and/or intended supervisor is available in a subsequent year. Requests will be considered on an individual basis, particularly in relation to non-UK/Irish applicants who may have experienced delays in obtaining an entry visa in time to commence their studies. Applications for deferral of University administered funding are not permitted.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you need to improve your English language skills before you enter this degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers a range of English language courses. These intensive and flexible courses are designed to improve your English ability for admission to this degree.
- [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English): an intensive English language and study skills course for successful university study at degree level.
- [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/digital-marketing-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English): a short intensive academic English course for students starting a degree programme at Queen's University Belfast and who need to improve their English.
For applicants from China Mainland, Queen's states under Borderline Cases: "We will consider students who have completed their degree with lower grades than those outlined in their offer letter." For many postgraduate taught programmes requiring a UK 2:1 standard, Chinese graduates will normally be accepted with a final average mark of up to **2% below the condition stated in the official offer letter**, assuming performance in key modules is appropriate. Where entry requirements are different, borderline cases will be considered at the discretion of the Academic Selector. Sometimes flexibility may be possible for applicants more than **2% below the target grade** when final results are known, at the discretion of the Academic Selector.
On completion of your degree, you should forward a copy of the following documents to intl.student@qub.ac.uk to confirm the award of your qualification and the overall grade:
- Official transcript (final version including all your grades)
- Bachelor degree Certificate
- Graduation Certificate
It is only on receipt of these documents that Queen's will be able to confirm your acceptance.
